newsitem.title: USA: Kohl's 5-week December same store sales up.
newsitem.headline: Kohl's 5-week December same store sales up.

text.p: Kohl's Corp said Thursday that same store sales for the five-week period ended January 4 rose 5.9 percent, excluding electronics.
Total sales of that period were up 16.4 percent to $436.0 million from $374.5 million.

Due to a shift in the calendar, the fiscal month ending dates are one week later this year than a year ago. On a calendar basis, matching the five weeks ended January 4, 1997 with the five weeks ended January 6, 1996, total sales increased 33 percent for the month, Kohl's said.
On an adjusted basis, comparable store sales increased 20.8 percent excluding electronics, it added.

"The results of the holiday season surpassed our expectations," William Kellogg, chairman, said in a statement. "Combining November and December, our comparable store sales increased 10.7 percent on a fiscal period basis and 15.6 percent on a calendar month basis."

Including the discontinued electronics sales, Kohl's said its comparable store sales for the holiday season increased 7.9 percent on a fiscal period basis and 12.8 percent on a calendar basis. This increase was on top of a 7.6 percent comparable store sales gain a year ago.

For the 11 months ended January 4, 1997, sales were up 24.6 percent compared with the year-to-date period ended December 30, 1996. On a comparable store basis, sales increased 10.8 percent excluding electronics.
